sourceMethodology: Regulatory minimums per OSFI Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR) 2026 guideline and Basel III global standards. D-SIB supervisory target reflects the Domestic Stability Buffer set by OSFI (0-4% of RWA, reviewed semi-annually each June/December); current DSB = 3.0% effective June 19, 2026.

metrics.label: Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) Ratio
metrics.description: Core equity capital as a percentage of risk-weighted assets. The primary measure of a bank's capital strength and loss-absorbing capacity.

metrics.label: Tier 1 Capital Ratio
metrics.description: CET1 plus Additional Tier 1 capital, as a percentage of risk-weighted assets.

metrics.label: Total Capital Ratio
metrics.description: Tier 1 plus Tier 2 capital, as a percentage of risk-weighted assets. Broadest regulatory capital adequacy measure.

metrics.label: Basel III Leverage Ratio
metrics.description: Tier 1 capital as a percentage of total (non-risk-weighted) exposure. Guards against excessive on- and off-balance-sheet leverage.

metrics.label: Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) Ratio
metrics.description: Capital and eligible long-term debt available to absorb losses in a resolution scenario, as a percentage of risk-weighted assets. Applies to Canada's D-SIBs.

metrics.label: TLAC Leverage Ratio
metrics.description: Total loss-absorbing capacity as a percentage of leverage ratio exposure — the non-risk-weighted companion to the TLAC ratio. Calculated under OSFI's TLAC guideline; OSFI requires Canada's D-SIBs to hold at least 7.25%.

metrics.label: Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR)
metrics.description: High-quality liquid assets available to cover net cash outflows over a 30-day stress scenario.

metrics.label: Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR)
metrics.description: Available stable funding relative to required stable funding over a one-year horizon. Measures structural, longer-term liquidity resilience.

metrics.label: Return on Equity (ROE)
metrics.description: Net income attributable to common shareholders as a percentage of average common shareholders' equity.

metrics.label: Return on Assets (ROA)
metrics.description: Quarterly net income annualised (x4) as a percentage of period-end total assets. Computed on one consistent basis for all six banks, because only BMO, CIBC and National Bank disclose an ROA and they do so on an average-assets basis.

metrics.label: Return on Tangible Common Equity (ROTCE)
metrics.description: Net income available to common shareholders as a percentage of average common equity less goodwill and intangible assets. Reported basis. Disclosed by RBC, BMO, Scotiabank and TD; CIBC and National Bank do not publish it.

metrics.label: Equity Multiplier (Avg Assets / Avg Equity)
metrics.description: Average total assets divided by average common equity — balance-sheet leverage, and the DuPont term linking ROA to ROE. Computed from two figures each issuer discloses in its financial supplement. Context-dependent rather than better-when-higher: more leverage lifts ROE but thins the equity cushion.

metrics.label: Dividend Payout Ratio
metrics.description: Common share dividends as a percentage of net income available to common shareholders. Context-dependent rather than better-when-higher: a higher payout returns more to shareholders but retains less capital. Bases differ by issuer — National Bank discloses a trailing four-quarter ratio, and Scotiabank publishes none quarterly, so its figures are computed from its own disclosed dividends and net income (the same formula reproduces Scotiabank's published annual payout exactly).

metrics.label: Net Interest Margin (NIM)
metrics.description: Net interest income as a percentage of average interest-earning assets.

metrics.label: Efficiency Ratio
metrics.description: Non-interest expense as a percentage of total revenue. Lower indicates better cost discipline.

metrics.label: Adjusted Operating Leverage
metrics.description: Adjusted revenue growth less adjusted non-interest expense growth. Positive means revenue is growing faster than costs. Disclosed quarterly by RBC, BMO, CIBC and National Bank; Scotiabank publishes it only annually and TD only qualitatively, so both are shown as not disclosed.

metrics.label: Loans as % of Total Assets
metrics.description: Gross loans as a percentage of total balance sheet assets — a proxy for balance sheet lending intensity vs. trading/securities/other assets.

metrics.label: Total Assets
metrics.description: Total balance sheet assets at period end, in billions of reporting currency.

metrics.label: Net Income
metrics.description: Net income attributable to shareholders for the quarter, in millions of reporting currency.

metrics.label: Adjusted Diluted EPS
metrics.description: Adjusted net income per diluted common share, as each issuer publishes it. Adjusted measures strip out each bank's own items of note, so the adjustments are not identical across the six even though every figure is the bank's own published number.

metrics.label: Loan-to-Deposit Ratio
metrics.description: Gross loans as a percentage of total deposits. A core funding-structure gauge: a ratio well above 100% signals reliance on non-deposit (wholesale) funding to support lending; a low ratio signals surplus deposit funding.

metrics.label: Wholesale Funding (% of Total Assets)
metrics.description: Wholesale funding (interbank deposits, wholesale/institutional deposit notes, covered bonds, securitization, senior/subordinated debt, repo) as a percentage of total assets. Lower generally indicates a more stable, less market-dependent funding profile.

metrics.label: Retail Deposits (% of Total Deposits)
metrics.description: Personal/retail deposits as a percentage of total deposits. Retail deposits are typically more stable and lower-cost than wholesale/commercial deposits.

metrics.label: Wholesale/Commercial Deposits (% of Total Deposits)
metrics.description: Wholesale, commercial, and institutional deposits as a percentage of total deposits.

metrics.label: Stable Deposits (% of Total Deposits, LCR Basis)
metrics.description: Deposits classified as 'stable' under Basel/OSFI LCR deposit-runoff categorization (e.g., fully insured, established relationship) as a percentage of total deposits — lower expected outflow rate in a 30-day stress scenario.

metrics.label: Less Stable Deposits (% of Total Deposits, LCR Basis)
metrics.description: Deposits classified as 'less stable' under Basel/OSFI LCR deposit-runoff categorization as a percentage of total deposits — higher expected outflow rate in a 30-day stress scenario.

metrics.label: Operational Deposits (% of Total Deposits)
metrics.description: Deposits tied to an operational relationship (clearing, custody, cash management) as a percentage of total deposits — these receive preferential (lower) LCR runoff rates due to their stickiness.

metrics.label: Non-Operational Deposits (% of Total Deposits)
metrics.description: Wholesale deposits with no operational relationship as a percentage of total deposits — these receive higher LCR runoff rates, reflecting greater flight risk in stress.

metrics.label: IRRBB — ΔEVE Sensitivity (% of Tier 1 Capital)
metrics.description: Change in Economic Value of Equity under the most adverse interest-rate shock the bank discloses, as a percentage of Tier 1 capital. OSFI's IRRBB 'outlier' test flags a bank for supervisory review if the full six-scenario measure exceeds 15%. All six Canadian D-SIBs disclose a +/-100bp parallel-shock version of this every quarter in their Reports to Shareholders (RBC and National show additional scenarios); the standardized six-scenario Basel/OSFI template is annual where disclosed. Values here use each bank's most-adverse disclosed scenario — see per-point notes.

metrics.label: IRRBB — ΔNII Sensitivity (12-Month)
metrics.description: Projected change in 12-month net interest income under a prescribed parallel interest rate shock (commonly +/-100bps), as a percentage of Tier 1 capital. All six Canadian D-SIBs disclose this every quarter in their Reports to Shareholders. Sign, shock direction, and scope vary by bank disclosure (some report the +100bp scenario, others the most-adverse) — see notes per data point.
